                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1230,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"## Architecture Overview\\n\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;mermaid\\nflowchart TD\\n    subgraph auth_flow [Authentication Flow]\\n        A[User clicks Google Login] --&amp;gt; B[Google OAuth]\\n        B --&amp;gt; C[Redirect back with Google identity]\\n        C --&amp;gt; D{Work email linked?}\\n        D --&amp;gt;|No| E[Prompt for work email]\\n        E --&amp;gt; F{Domain is czu.cz?}\\n        F --&amp;gt;|No| G[Show domain error]\\n        G --&amp;gt; E\\n        F --&amp;gt;|Yes| H[Send OTP to work email]\\n        H --&amp;gt; I[User enters OTP]\\n        I --&amp;gt; J[Link work email identity]\\n        J --&amp;gt; K{Email in approved list?}\\n        D --&amp;gt;|Yes| K\\n        K --&amp;gt;|No| L[Pending Approval Page]\\n        K --&amp;gt;|Yes| M[Grant Full Access]\\n    end\\n\\n    subgraph request_flow [Request Validation]\\n        N[Incoming Request] --&amp;gt; O[Middleware checks JWT]\\n        O --&amp;gt; P{Has verified_work_email?}\\n        P --&amp;gt;|No| Q[Redirect to verify email]\\n        P --&amp;gt;|Yes| R{is_approved claim?}\\n         [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1447,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"  created_by uuid references auth.users(id),\","

                  "lineNumber": 1478,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"  id uuid primary key references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,\","

                  "lineNumber": 2711,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"  is_approved boolean;\\nbegin\\n  -- Get user profile data\\n  select role, verified_work_email into user_role, work_email\\n  from public.user_profiles\\n  where id = (event-&amp;gt;&amp;gt;'user_id')::uuid;\\n\\n  -- Check if work email is in approved list\\n  select exists(\\n    select 1 from public.approved_emails where email = work_email\\n  ) into is_approved;\\n\\n  -- Build custom claims\\n  claims := coalesce(event-&amp;gt;'claims', '{}'::jsonb);\\n  claims := jsonb_set(claims, '{role}', to_jsonb(coalesce(user_role, 'user')));\\n  claims := jsonb_set(claims, '{verified_work_email}', to_jsonb(work_email));\\n  claims := jsonb_set(claims, '{is_approved}', to_jsonb(coalesce(is_approved, false)));\\n\\n  return jsonb_set(event, '{claims}', claims);\\nend;\\n$$;\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\n\\nEnable in config:\\n\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;toml\\n[auth.hook.custom_access_token]\\nenabled = true\\nuri = \\\"pg-functions://postgres/public/custom_access_token_hook\\\"\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\n\\n## Development &amp;amp; Testing with S [... omitted end of long line]"

        "contents": "-- Grant execute permission to authenticated and anonymous roles\n-- This allows the trigger to execute when users update their email\ngrant execute on function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger() to authenticated;\ngrant execute on function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger() to anon;\n\n-- Create trigger on auth.users table\n-- This fires BEFORE any update to email or email_change columns\n-- The trigger cannot be bypassed - it runs at the database level\ndrop trigger if exists validate_czu_email_domain_trigger on auth.users;\n\ncreate trigger validate_czu_email_domain_trigger\nbefore update of email, email_change on auth.users\nfor each row\nexecute function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger();\n\n-- Add comment explaining the security model\ncomment on function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger() is \n'Server-side trigger function that validates email domains at the database level. Uses SECURITY DEFINER to access auth.users table. Cannot be bypassed by client-side code. Entities &amp; Schemas\n\n### Example: &#96;users&#96;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate table users (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  email text unique not null,\n  phone text unique,\n  created_at timestamptz default now()\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Example: &#96;subscriptions&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate table subscriptions (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  user_id uuid references users(id),\n  stripe_customer_id text,\n  stripe_subscription_id text,\n  status text check (status in ('active','canceled','past_due')),\n  created_at timestamptz default now()\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n\\[Add more entities as needed: &#96;messages&#96;, &#96;tasks&#96;, &#96;reminders&#96;, etc.]\n\n---\n\n## 4. Features\n\n### 4.1 Onboarding &amp; Payment\n\n* **Signup:** \\[Auth provider]\n* **Phone Verification:**\n\n  * Input: &#96;{ phone_number }&#96;\n  * Output: &#96;{ success: true, otp_sent: true }&#96;\n* **Payment:** Stripe/PayPal/etc → subscription sync\n\n### 4.2 Channels / Interfaces\n\n#### Web Chat\n\n* Input: &#96;{ user_id, message }&#96;\n* Output: &#96;{ status: \"stored\", assistant_reply }&#96;\n* Flow:\n\n  1.         "contents": "-- Migration: Restrict signups to Google OAuth only\n-- Purpose: Blocks email/password signups and OTP signups, only allows Google OAuth\n-- This ensures all new accounts must be created via Google OAuth\n\n-- Create before_user_created hook in public schema to only allow Google OAuth signups\n-- Blocks email/password signups and other OAuth providers\n-- Uses public schema instead of auth schema\ncreate or replace function public.before_user_created_hook(event jsonb)\nreturns jsonb\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer\nset search_path = ''\nas $$\ndeclare\n  v_provider text;\n  v_encrypted_password text;\n  v_app_metadata jsonb;\n  v_identity jsonb;\n  v_has_google_identity boolean := false;\nbegin\n  -- Extract encrypted_password first (most reliable indicator of password signup)\n  v_encrypted_password := event-&gt;'user'-&gt;&gt;'encrypted_password';\n  \n  -- Block password-based signups immediately (they have encrypted_password)\n  if v_encrypted_password is not null then\n    raise exception 'Password-based signups are not allowed. Please use Google OAuth to sign in.';\n  end if;\n  \n  -- Extract provider from multiple possible locations\n  -- 1. raw_user_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'provider'\n  v_provider := event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'raw_user_meta_data'-&gt;&gt;'provider';\n  \n  -- 2. app_metadata-&gt;&gt;'provider'\n  v_app_metadata := event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'app_metadata';\n  if v_provider is null and v_app_metadata is not null then\n    v_provider := v_app_metadata-&gt;&gt;'provider';\n  end if;\n  \n  -- 3. Check identities array for Google provider (most reliable for OAuth)\n  if event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'identities' is not null then\n    for v_identity in \n      select value from jsonb_array_elements(event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'identities')\n    loop\n      if v_identity-&gt;&gt;'provider' = 'google' then\n        v_has_google_identity := true;\n        exit;\n      end if;\n    end loop;\n  end if;\n  \n  -- Allow Google OAuth signups (check both provider variable and identities array)\n  if v_provider = 'google' or v_has_google_identity then\n    return event;\n  end if;\n  \n  -- If we reach here, it's not a Google OAuth signup and not a password signup\n  -- This must be an OTP or other email-based signup attempt",

        "contents": "-- Migration: Server-side CZU email domain validation\n-- Purpose: Ensures that email addresses being changed must end with @pef.czu.cz or @studenti.czu.cz\n-- This uses SECURITY DEFINER to create a trigger on auth.users table for true server-side enforcement\n-- The trigger runs at the database level and cannot be bypassed by client-side code\n\n-- Create validation trigger function with SECURITY DEFINER\n-- SECURITY DEFINER allows the function to access auth.users table even when called by regular users\n-- This provides true server-side enforcement at the Supabase database level\ncreate or replace function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger()\nreturns trigger\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer\nset search_path = public, auth\nas $$\ndeclare\n  v_email text;\n  v_email_change text;\n  v_domain text;\nbegin\n  -- Only validate on UPDATE (email changes), not INSERT (new user creation)",

        "contents": "student: 0,\n  team_leader: 1,\n  coach: 2,\n  admin: 3,\n} as const;\n\nexport const hasMinimumRole = (userRole: ProfileRole, requiredRole: ProfileRole): boolean =&gt; {\n  return ROLE_HIERARCHY[userRole] &gt;= ROLE_HIERARCHY[requiredRole];\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Supabase Configuration Changes\n\nUpdate [&#96;supabase/config.toml&#96;](supabase/config.toml):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;toml\n[auth]\nenable_manual_linking = true        # Required for work email linking\nenable_anonymous_sign_ins = false   # Block anonymous access\n\n[auth.email]\nenable_signup = false               # Block direct email/password signup\nenable_confirmations = false        # We use OTP for work email, not signup confirmation\n\n[auth.external.google]\nenabled = true\nclient_id = \"env(GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID)\"\nsecret = \"env(GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET)\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Profile Verification (Next.js Middleware)\n\nAll verification logic lives in Next.js middleware, not in Supabase:\n\n- **Profile Linked**: Check &#96;profiles.user_id&#96; matches current auth.user.id\n- **Access Active**: Check &#96;profiles.removed_access IS NULL&#96;\n- **User Role**: Read &#96;profiles.role&#96; column (student, team_leader, coach, admin)\n\nThis approach:\n\n- Keeps all business logic in Next.js (single source of truth)\n- Allows real-time updates (e.g., instant access revocation)\n- Admin pre-creates profiles, users link via work email verification\n- Supabase only handles auth + data storage (no custom hooks or functions)\n\n## Development &amp; Testing with Supabase MCP\n\nThe project has a &#96;supabase/&#96; directory with Supabase MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration available for:\n\n1. **Running migrations**: Apply and test database schema changes locally\n2. **Debugging auth flow**: Inspect user sessions and profile data\n3. **Testing verification logic**: Query profiles and teams tables\n\n**Useful MCP commands for development:**\n\n- Verify RLS policies by querying as different user roles\n- Seed test data into profiles and teams tables\n- Inspect auth.users and profiles tables\n- Test profile linking and access revocation queries\n\n## Key Security Features",

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./.cursor/rules/create-rls-policies.mdc",

        },
        "contents": "### &#96;auth.jwt()&#96;\n\nReturns the JWT of the user making the request. Anything that you store in the user's &#96;raw_app_meta_data&#96; column or the &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; column will be accessible using this function. It's important to know the distinction between these two:\n\n- &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; - can be updated by the authenticated user using the &#96;supabase.auth.update()&#96; function. It is not a good place to store authorization data.\n- &#96;raw_app_meta_data&#96; - cannot be updated by the user, so it's a good place to store authorization data.\n\nThe &#96;auth.jwt()&#96; function is extremely versatile. For example, if you store some team data inside &#96;app_metadata&#96;, you can use it to determine whether a particular user belongs to a team. For example, if this was an array of IDs:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"User is in team\"\non my_table\nto authenticated\nusing ( team_id in (select auth.jwt() -&gt; 'app_metadata' -&gt; 'teams'));\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### MFA\n\nThe &#96;auth.jwt()&#96; function can be used to check for [Multi-Factor Authentication](mdc:docs/guides/auth/auth-mfa#enforce-rules-for-mfa-logins). For example, you could restrict a user from updating their profile unless they have at least 2 levels of authentication (Assurance Level 2):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Restrict updates.\"\non profiles\nas restrictive\nfor update\nto authenticated using (\n  (select auth.jwt()-&gt;&gt;'aal') = 'aal2'\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## RLS performance recommendations\n\nEvery authorization system has an impact on performance. While row level security is powerful, the performance impact is important to keep in mind. This is especially true for queries that scan every row in a table - like many &#96;select&#96; operations, including those using limit, offset, and ordering.\n\nBased on a series of [tests](mdc:https:/github.com/GaryAustin1/RLS-Performance), we have a few recommendations for RLS:\n\n### Add indexes\n\nMake sure you've added [indexes](mdc:docs/guides/database/postgres/indexes) on any columns used within the Policies which are not already indexed (or primary keys). For a Policy like this:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "### &#96;auth.jwt()&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 123
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 124
          },
          {
            "text": "Returns the JWT of the user making the request. Anything that you store in the user's &#96;raw_app_meta_data&#96; column or the &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; column will be accessible using this function. It's important to know the distinction between these two:",
            "lineNumber": 125
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 126
          },
          {
            "text": "- &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; - can be updated by the authenticated user using the &#96;supabase.auth.update()&#96; function. It is not a good place to store authorization data.",
            "lineNumber": 127
          },
          {
            "text": "- &#96;raw_app_meta_data&#96; - cannot be updated by the user, so it's a good place to store authorization data.",
            "lineNumber": 128
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 129
          },
          {
            "text": "The &#96;auth.jwt()&#96; function is extremely versatile. For example, if you store some team data inside &#96;app_metadata&#96;, you can use it to determine whether a particular user belongs to a team. For example, if this was an array of IDs:",
            "lineNumber": 130
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 131
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql",
            "lineNumber": 132
          },
          {
            "text": "create policy \"User is in team\"",
            "lineNumber": 133
          },
          {
            "text": "on my_table",
            "lineNumber": 134
          },
          {
            "text": "to authenticated",
            "lineNumber": 135
          },
          {
            "text": "using ( team_id in (select auth.jwt() -&gt; 'app_metadata' -&gt; 'teams'));",
            "lineNumber": 136
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 137
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 138
          },
          {
            "text": "### MFA",
            "lineNumber": 139
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 140
          },
          {
            "text": "The &#96;auth.jwt()&#96; function can be used to check for [Multi-Factor Authentication](mdc:docs/guides/auth/auth-mfa#enforce-rules-for-mfa-logins). For example, you could restrict a user from updating their profile unless they have at least 2 levels of authentication (Assurance Level 2):",
            "lineNumber": 141
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 142
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql",
            "lineNumber": 143
          },
          {
            "text": "create policy \"Restrict updates.\"",
            "lineNumber": 144
          },
          {
            "text": "on profiles",
            "lineNumber": 145
          },
          {
            "text": "as restrictive",
            "lineNumber": 146
          },
          {
            "text": "for update",
            "lineNumber": 147
          },
          {
            "text": "to authenticated using (",
            "lineNumber": 148
          },
          {
            "text": "  (select auth.jwt()-&gt;&gt;'aal') = 'aal2'",
            "lineNumber": 149
          },
          {
            "text": ");",
            "lineNumber": 150
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 151
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 152
          },
          {
            "text": "## RLS performance recommendations",
            "lineNumber": 153
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 154
          },
          {
            "text": "Every authorization system has an impact on performance. While row level security is powerful, the performance impact is important to keep in mind. This is especially true for queries that scan every row in a table - like many &#96;select&#96; operations, including those using limit, offset, and ordering.",
            "lineNumber": 155
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 156
          },
          {
            "text": "Based on a series of [tests](mdc:https:/github.com/GaryAustin1/RLS-Performance), we have a few recommendations for RLS:",
            "lineNumber": 157
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 158
          },
          {
            "text": "### Add indexes",
            "lineNumber": 159
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 160
          },
          {
            "text": "Make sure you've added [indexes](mdc:docs/guides/database/postgres/indexes) on any columns used within the Policies which are not already indexed (or primary keys). For a Policy like this:",
            "lineNumber": 161
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 162
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql",
            "lineNumber": 163
          },
          {
            "text": "create policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table",
            "lineNumber": 164
          }
        ]
      },

        "contents": "- Inspect auth.users and profiles tables\n- Test profile linking and access revocation queries\n\n## Key Security Features\n\n### Supabase (Data Layer)\n\n2. **Database Constraints**:\n\n   - Domain constraint ensures only valid CZU domains in profiles\n   - Unique constraints on work_email, user_id\n\n### Next.js (Application Layer)\n\n1. **Middleware Verification**:\n\n   - Queries &#96;profiles&#96; table for linked user_id\n   - Checks &#96;removed_access&#96; is null for active access\n   - Enforces role-based route protection\n   - Real-time verification (instant access revocation)\n\n2. **Domain Validation** (in server actions):\n\n   - Client-side validation for UX (immediate feedback)\n   - Server-side validation before sending OTP\n   - Validates email format and CZU domain\n\n3. **Access Management** (in server actions):\n\n   - Admin sets &#96;removed_access&#96; timestamp and &#96;removed_access_by&#96; profile\n   - Immediate effect on next request\n   - Audit trail of who revoked access and when\n\n## Authentication Flow Details\n\n### Step 1: Google Login\n\nUser clicks Google login button, Supabase handles OAuth flow.\n\n### Step 2: Work Email Input with Domain Validation\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Validate domain before sending OTP\nif (!isValidWorkEmailDomain(workEmail)) {\n  throw new Error('Email must be @studenti.czu.cz or @pef.czu.cz');\n}\n\n// Send OTP to work email (only after domain validation passes)\nconst { error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({\n  email: workEmail,\n  options: { shouldCreateUser: false }\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 3: OTP Verification and Profile Linking\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// After user enters OTP, verify it\nconst { error } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp({\n  email: workEmail,\n  token: otpCode,\n  type: 'email'\n});\n\n// Check if profile exists for this work email\nconst { data: profile } = await supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .select('id')\n  .eq('work_email', workEmail)\n  .single();\n\nif (!profile) {\n  // No profile exists - redirect to pending approval",

        "contents": "\"use client\";\n\nimport { useState, useEffect } from \"react\";\nimport { createClient } from \"@/lib/supabase/client\";\nimport { GoogleLoginButton } from \"@/components/google-login-button\";\nimport { Button } from \"@/components/ui/button\";\nimport { Input } from \"@/components/ui/input\";\nimport { Label } from \"@/components/ui/label\";\nimport {\n  Card,\n  CardContent,\n  CardDescription,\n  CardHeader,\n  CardTitle,\n} from \"@/components/ui/card\";\nimport { Badge } from \"@/components/ui/badge\";\n\n/**\n * Test page for verifying auth restrictions\n * Tests:\n * - Google OAuth signup (should work)\n * - Email/password signup (should be blocked)\n * - OTP email signup (should be blocked)\n * - Email identity addition (should validate CZU domain)\n */\nexport default function AuthTestPage() {\n  const [user, setUser] = useState&lt;any&gt;(null);\n  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);\n  const [testResults, setTestResults] = useState&lt;{\n    emailPassword?: { success: boolean; message: string };\n    emailOTP?: { success: boolean; message: string };\n    emailIdentity?: { success: boolean; message: string };\n  }&gt;({});\n\n  const supabase = createClient();\n\n  useEffect(() =&gt; {\n    checkUser();\n    supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange(() =&gt; {\n      checkUser();\n    });\n  }, []);\n\n  const checkUser = async () =&gt; {\n    const {\n      data: { user: currentUser },\n    } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\n    setUser(currentUser);\n    setLoading(false);\n  };\n\n  const testEmailPasswordSignup = async (e: React.FormEvent&lt;HTMLFormElement&gt;)\n;\n}",

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./lib/auth-helpers.ts",
        "range": {

            "column": 1
          }
        },
        "contents": "/**\n * Checks if the authenticated user has an email identity linked\n * (not just OAuth providers like Google)\n * @returns true if user has an email identity, false otherwise\n */\nexport async function hasEmailIdentity(): Promise&lt;boolean&gt; {\n  const supabase = await createClient();\n  const { data: { user }, error } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\n\n  if (error || !user) {\n    return false;\n  }\n\n  // Check if user has an email identity (not just OAuth)\n  // User identities include: email, google, etc.\n  // We need at least one email identity\n  const identities = user.identities || [];\n  \n  // Check if any identity is an email identity (not OAuth)\n  return identities.some(\n    (identity) =&gt; identity.provider === \"email\"\n  );\n}",

      "codeBlock": {

          }
        },
        "contents": "if (!profile) {\n  // No profile exists - redirect to pending approval\n  redirect('/auth/pending-approval');\n}\n\n// Link profile to current user\nconst { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\nawait supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .update({ \n    user_id: user.id,\n    picture: user.user_metadata.avatar_url  // Default to Google picture\n  })\n  .eq('work_email', workEmail);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 4: Middleware Validation\n\nQuery database for profile linked to current auth.user and check &#96;removed_access IS NULL&#96; on every request to protected routes.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Middleware check\nconst { data: profile } = await supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .select('id, role, removed_access')\n  .eq('user_id', user.id)\n  .single();\n\nif (!profile) redirect('/auth/verify-work-email');\nif (profile.removed_access) redirect('/auth/access-revoked');\n// User has active access, continue...\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Estimated Complexity\n\n| Task | Complexity | Lines of Code |\n\n|------|------------|---------------|\n\n| Delete old auth files | Trivial | -500 lines |\n\n| Security lockdown config | Trivial | ~20 lines TOML |\n\n| Database migration | Low | ~50 lines SQL (profiles, teams, indexes) |\n\n| Constants + validation | Trivial | ~25 lines |\n\n| Server actions (business logic) | Medium | ~80 lines |\n\n| Middleware update | Medium | ~50 lines (includes DB queries) |\n\n| Google login page | Low | ~30 lines |\n\n| Work email form + linking | Medium | ~120 lines |\n\n| Admin UI (profiles + teams) | Medium | ~150 lines |\n\n**Total new code**: ~525 lines (vs ~500 lines deleted)\n\n## Separation of Concerns\n\n### Supabase (Auth + Storage Only)\n\n- **Authentication**: Google OAuth flow, session management, OTP emails\n- **Database**: Store profiles, teams data with RLS for row-level access control\n- **No business logic**: No custom hooks, no stored procedures, no triggers for business rules\n\n### Next.js (All Business Logic)\n\n- **Middleware**: Profile verification, access checks, role-based routing\n- **Server Actions**: Profile linking, access revocation, team management",

        "contents": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table\nto authenticated\nusing ( (select auth.uid()) = user_id );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou can add an index like:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate index userid\non test_table\nusing btree (user_id);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Call functions with &#96;select&#96;\n\nYou can use &#96;select&#96; statement to improve policies that use functions. For example, instead of this:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table\nto authenticated\nusing ( auth.uid() = user_id );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou can do:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table\nto authenticated\nusing ( (select auth.uid()) = user_id );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis method works well for JWT functions like &#96;auth.uid()&#96; and &#96;auth.jwt()&#96; as well as &#96;security definer&#96; Functions. Wrapping the function causes an &#96;initPlan&#96; to be run by the Postgres optimizer, which allows it to \"cache\" the results per-statement, rather than calling the function on each row.\n\nCaution: You can only use this technique if the results of the query or function do not change based on the row data.\n\n### Minimize joins\n\nYou can often rewrite your Policies to avoid joins between the source and the target table. Instead, try to organize your policy to fetch all the relevant data from the target table into an array or set, then you can use an &#96;IN&#96; or &#96;ANY&#96; operation in your filter.\n\nFor example, this is an example of a slow policy which joins the source &#96;test_table&#96; to the target &#96;team_user&#96;:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access records belonging to their teams\" on test_table\nto authenticated\nusing (\n  (select auth.uid()) in (\n    select user_id\n    from team_user\n    where team_user.team_id = team_id -- joins to the source \"test_table.team_id\"\n  )\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nWe can rewrite this to avoid this join, and instead select the filter criteria into a set:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access records belonging to their teams\" on test_table\nto authenticated\nusing (\n  team_id in (\n    select team_id\n    from team_user",

          },
          {
            "text": "using ( (select auth.uid()) = user_id );",

            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",

          {
            "text": "on test_table",
            "lineNumber": 173
          },
          {
            "text": "using btree (user_id);",
            "lineNumber": 174
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 175
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 176
          },
          {
            "text": "### Call functions with &#96;select&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 177
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 178
          },
          {
            "text": "You can use &#96;select&#96; statement to improve policies that use functions. For example, instead of this:",
            "lineNumber": 179
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 180
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql",
            "lineNumber": 181
          },
          {
            "text": "create policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table",
            "lineNumber": 182
          },
          {
            "text": "to authenticated",
            "lineNumber": 183
          },
          {
            "text": "using ( auth.uid() = user_id );",
            "lineNumber": 184
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 185
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 186
          },
          {
            "text": "You can do:",
            "lineNumber": 187
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 188
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql",
            "lineNumber": 189
          },
          {
            "text": "create policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table",
            "lineNumber": 190
          },
          {
            "text": "to authenticated",
            "lineNumber": 191
          },
          {
            "text": "using ( (select auth.uid()) = user_id );",
            "lineNumber": 192
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 193
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 194
          },
          {
            "text": "This method works well for JWT functions like &#96;auth.uid()&#96; and &#96;auth.jwt()&#96; as well as &#96;security definer&#96; Functions. Wrapping the function causes an &#96;initPlan&#96; to be run by the Postgres optimizer, which allows it to \"cache\" the results per-statement, rather than calling the function on each row.",
            "lineNumber": 195
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 196
          },
          {
            "text": "Caution: You can only use this technique if the results of the query or function do not change based on the row data.",
            "lineNumber": 197
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 198
          },
          {
            "text": "### Minimize joins",
            "lineNumber": 199
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 200
          },
          {
            "text": "You can often rewrite your Policies to avoid joins between the source and the target table. Instead, try to organize your policy to fetch all the relevant data from the target table into an array or set, then you can use an &#96;IN&#96; or &#96;ANY&#96; operation in your filter.",
            "lineNumber": 201
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 202
          },
          {
            "text": "For example, this is an example of a slow policy which joins the source &#96;test_table&#96; to the target &#96;team_user&#96;:",
            "lineNumber": 203
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 204
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql",
            "lineNumber": 205
          },
          {
            "text": "create policy \"Users can access records belonging to their teams\" on test_table",
            "lineNumber": 206
          },
          {
            "text": "to authenticated",
            "lineNumber": 207
          },
          {
            "text": "using (",
            "lineNumber": 208
          },
          {
            "text": "  (select auth.uid()) in (",
            "lineNumber": 209
          },
          {
            "text": "    select user_id",
            "lineNumber": 210
          },
          {
            "text": "    from team_user",
            "lineNumber": 211
          },
          {
            "text": "    where team_user.team_id = team_id -- joins to the source \"test_table.team_id\"",
            "lineNumber": 212
          },
          {
            "text": "  )",
            "lineNumber": 213
          },
          {
            "text": ");",
            "lineNumber": 214
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 215
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 216
          },
          {
            "text": "We can rewrite this to avoid this join, and instead select the filter criteria into a set:",
            "lineNumber": 217
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 218
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql",
            "lineNumber": 219
          },
          {
            "text": "create policy \"Users can access records belonging to their teams\" on test_table",
            "lineNumber": 220
          },
          {
            "text": "to authenticated",
            "lineNumber": 221
          },
          {
            "text": "using (",
            "lineNumber": 222
          },
          {
            "text": "  team_id in (",
            "lineNumber": 223
          },
          {
            "text": "    select team_id",
            "lineNumber": 224
          },
          {
            "text": "    from team_user",
            "lineNumber": 225
          }
        ]
      },
      "score": 0.21496060490608215

        "contents": "  v_email_change text;\n  v_domain text;\nbegin\n  -- Only validate on UPDATE (email changes), not INSERT (new user creation)\n  -- This allows OAuth signups (Google, etc.) to create accounts with any email\n  if tg_op != 'UPDATE' then\n    return NEW;\n  end if;\n\n  -- Validate email_change field (where Supabase stores new email during change process)\n  -- This applies to ALL users (both OAuth and email-only)\n  -- OAuth users can sign up, but when they try to add an email identity, it must be CZU domain\n  if OLD.email_change is distinct from NEW.email_change then\n    v_email_change := NEW.email_change;\n    \n    -- Skip validation if email_change is null or empty\n    if v_email_change is not null and v_email_change != '' then\n      -- Extract domain from email_change (everything after @)\n      v_domain := lower(split_part(v_email_change, '@', 2));\n      \n      -- Validate domain is one of the allowed CZU domains\n      -- This applies to all users, including OAuth users trying to add email identity\n      if v_domain not in ('pef.czu.cz', 'studenti.czu.cz') then\n        raise exception 'Email must end with @pef.czu.cz or @studenti.czu.cz. Provided domain: %', v_domain;\n      end if;\n    end if;\n  end if;\n\n  -- Validate email field if it changed\n  -- For OAuth users: validate when they're changing from OAuth email to a new email\n  -- For email-only users: always validate\n  if OLD.email is distinct from NEW.email then\n    v_email := NEW.email;\n    \n    -- Skip validation if email is null or empty\n    if v_email is not null and v_email != '' then\n      -- Extract domain from email (everything after @)\n      v_domain := lower(split_part(v_email, '@', 2));\n      \n      -- Validate domain is one of the allowed CZU domains\n      -- This applies to all users when changing primary email\n      if v_domain not in ('pef.czu.cz', 'studenti.czu.cz') then\n        raise exception 'Email must end with @pef.czu.cz or @studenti.czu.cz. Provided domain: %', v_domain;\n      end if;\n    end if;\n  end if;\n\n  return NEW;\nend;\n$$;\n\n-- Grant execute permission to authenticated and anonymous roles\n-- This allows the trigger to execute when users update their email",

Use environment variable substitution instead:\nauth_token = \"env(SUPABASE_AUTH_SMS_TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN)\"\n\n# Multi-factor-authentication is available to Supabase Pro plan.\n[auth.mfa]\n# Control how many MFA factors can be enrolled at once per user.\nmax_enrolled_factors = 10\n\n# Control MFA via App Authenticator (TOTP)\n[auth.mfa.totp]\nenroll_enabled = false\nverify_enabled = false\n\n# Configure MFA via Phone Messaging\n[auth.mfa.phone]\nenroll_enabled = false\nverify_enabled = false\notp_length = 8\ntemplate = \"Your code is {{ .Code }}\"\nmax_frequency = \"5s\"\n\n# Configure MFA via WebAuthn\n# [auth.mfa.web_authn]\n# enroll_enabled = true\n# verify_enabled = true\n\n# Use an external OAuth provider.         "contents": "end if;\n  \n  -- If we reach here, it's not a Google OAuth signup and not a password signup\n  -- This must be an OTP or other email-based signup attempt\n  raise exception 'Only Google OAuth signups are allowed. Please use Google to sign in.';\nend;\n$$;\n\n-- Grant execute permission (needed for hook execution)\ngrant execute on function public.before_user_created_hook(jsonb) to authenticated;\ngrant execute on function public.before_user_created_hook(jsonb) to anon;\n\n-- Note: Also update supabase/config.toml:\n-- [auth.email]\n-- enable_signup = false\n--\n-- [auth.hook.before_user_created]\n-- enabled = true\n-- uri = \"pg-functions://postgres/public/before_user_created_hook\"",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "end if;",
            "lineNumber": 54
          },
          {
            "text": "  ",
            "lineNumber": 55
          },
          {
            "text": "  -- If we reach here, it's not a Google OAuth signup and not a password signup",
            "lineNumber": 56
          },
          {
            "text": "  -- This must be an OTP or other email-based signup attempt",
            "lineNumber": 57
          },
          {
            "text": "  raise exception 'Only Google OAuth signups are allowed. Please use Google to sign in.';",
            "lineNumber": 58
          },
          {
            "text": "end;",
            "lineNumber": 59
          },
          {
            "text": "$$;",
            "lineNumber": 60
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 61
          },
          {
            "text": "-- Grant execute permission (needed for hook execution)",
            "lineNumber": 62

          {
            "text": "grant execute on function public.before_user_created_hook(jsonb) to authenticated;",

          {
            "text": "-- Note: Also update supabase/config.toml:",

        "contents": "---\ndescription: Guidelines for writing Postgres Row Level Security policies\nalwaysApply: false\n---\n\n# Database: Create RLS policies\n\nYou're a Supabase Postgres expert in writing row level security policies. Your purpose is to generate a policy with the constraints given by the user. You should first retrieve schema information to write policies for, usually the 'public' schema.\n\nThe output should use the following instructions:\n\n- The generated SQL must be valid SQL.\n- You can use only CREATE POLICY or ALTER POLICY queries, no other queries are allowed.\n- Always use double apostrophe in SQL strings (eg. 'Night''s watch')\n- You can add short explanations to your messages.\n- The result should be a valid markdown. The SQL code should be wrapped in &#96;&#96;&#96; (including sql language tag).\n- Always use \"auth.uid()\" instead of \"current_user\".\n- SELECT policies should always have USING but not WITH CHECK\n- INSERT policies should always have WITH CHECK but not USING\n- UPDATE policies should always have WITH CHECK and most often have USING\n- DELETE policies should always have USING but not WITH CHECK\n- Don't use &#96;FOR ALL&#96;. Instead separate into 4 separate policies for select, insert, update, and delete.\n- The policy name should be short but detailed text explaining the policy, enclosed in double quotes.\n- Always put explanations as separate text. Never use inline SQL comments.\n- If the user asks for something that's not related to SQL policies, explain to the user\n  that you can only help with policies.\n- Discourage &#96;RESTRICTIVE&#96; policies and encourage &#96;PERMISSIVE&#96; policies, and explain why.\n\nThe output should look like this:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\nCREATE POLICY \"My descriptive policy.\" ON books FOR INSERT to authenticated USING ( (select auth.uid()) = author_id ) WITH ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nSince you are running in a Supabase environment, take note of these Supabase-specific additions below.\n\n## Authenticated and unauthenticated roles\n\nSupabase maps every request to one of the roles:\n\n- &#96;anon&#96;: an unauthenticated request (the user is not logged in)\n- &#96;authenticated&#96;: an authenticated request (the user is logged in)",

Here’s what you can access from `auth.id` in Supabase:

## 1. **From Client Methods** (JavaScript/TypeScript)

### `supabase.auth.getUser()` or `supabase.auth.getClaims()`

Returns a user object with:

```typescript
{
  id: string,                    // UUID - the auth.id
  email: string,                 // User's email
  phone: string | null,          // Phone number if set
  email_confirmed_at: string | null,
  phone_confirmed_at: string | null,
  confirmed_at: string | null,   // When email or phone was confirmed
  last_sign_in_at: string | null,
  app_metadata: {
    provider: string,            // First signup provider (e.g., "google")
    providers: string[]          // All available login methods
  },
  user_metadata: {
    // Custom metadata + provider data (e.g., Google avatar_url, name)
    avatar_url?: string,
    name?: string,
    // ... other provider-specific fields
  },
  identities: [
    {
      id: string,
      provider: string,          // "email", "google", etc.
      // ... other identity fields
    }
  ]
}
```

## 2. **From Database** (`auth.users` table)

You can query `auth.users` directly in SQL (e.g., in migrations, functions, or with service role):

```sql
SELECT 
  id,
  aud,
  role,                    -- Postgres role for RLS
  email,
  email_confirmed_at,
  phone,
  phone_confirmed_at,
  confirmed_at,
  last_sign_in_at,
  app_metadata,            -- JSONB
  user_metadata,           -- JSONB
  raw_user_meta_data,      -- JSONB
  created_at,
  updated_at,
  email_change,
  email_change_token,
  email_change_sent_at,
  recovery_sent_at,
  new_email,
  invited_at,
  action_link,
  encrypted_password,
  -- ... other internal fields
FROM auth.users
WHERE id = 'user-uuid-here';
```

## 3. **In Your Codebase**

From your code:

```typescript
// From lib/auth-helpers.ts - accessing user.identities
const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();
const identities = user?.identities || [];

// From components/auth-button.tsx - accessing user.email
const { data } = await supabase.auth.getClaims();
const user = data?.claims;
// user.email is available

// From app/auth/test/page.tsx - accessing multiple fields
user.id
user.email
user.identities
```

## 4. **Important Limitations**

- `auth.users` is not exposed via the auto-generated Supabase API for security
- To expose user data via API, create a `public.users` table and sync it (as in your plan)
- Use `auth.uid()` in RLS policies to reference the current user's ID
- Access `auth.users` directly only with service role or in database functions/triggers

## 5. **Common Use Cases**

```typescript
// Get current user ID
const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();
const userId = user?.id;

// Check if user has email identity
const hasEmail = user?.identities?.some(id => id.provider === "email");

// Access user metadata (from OAuth providers)
const avatarUrl = user?.user_metadata?.avatar_url;
const name = user?.user_metadata?.name;

// Check email confirmation status
const isEmailConfirmed = !!user?.email_confirmed_at;
```

In your codebase, you're using `auth.id` to link `profiles.user_id` to `auth.users(id)`, which is the standard pattern for connecting Supabase auth to your application data.
